question: Can supervised, independently calibrated boundary-state credits correct the systematic teacher error seen in the uncalibrated pilot?
declared_after: Inspection of the prospectively locked 2027 development nomination audit for uncalibrated boundary coverage; the method did not materially separate anchored and local candidate precision.
state_fit: Ridge multinomial logit with a 0.01 penalty on standardized slopes and equal total weight per calibration patient.
proposal_audit: Using the same existing labeled selection-calibration cases, compare ordered versus slice-local multinomial state prediction, top-50 adjacent absence nominations, and realized class states among 80 queries per seed and fold.
label_roles: Use the even-indexed six original calibration patients to fit selection-state models; the odd-indexed six set final detection thresholds for every comparison arm. All roles are patient-disjoint within each fold. Dense reference consumption remains 160 training masks plus the original separate calibration masks. The controls are scored at the same six-patient detection thresholds.
primary: Patient-macro small-positive recall at retrospective 20% all-absence FPR, calibrated ordered coverage versus image difference; separately report improvement in realized adjacent absence and small label yield.
secondary_metrics: false positive rate and small recall at independent detection-calibration thresholds
scope: Exploratory follow-up. The previously observed 50 official ACDC cases are reused for locked retrospective evaluation, never for fitting, selection or further rule adjustment.
